component.name: HorsePower
component.summary: See how much electricity this computer is using

description.p: HorsePower reads the energy counters built into Intel and AMD processors and shows the power your machine is drawing right now, a breakdown of where that power goes, what it has used today, and what it has used since it was installed.

The breakdown separates the CPU package, the graphics card, memory, storage and the rest of the system. It only lists a component when your machine can actually measure it, so an unmeasurable part is left out rather than shown as zero.

A small background service samples the counter once a second and keeps a local log, so the totals stay correct even when the window is closed or the machine reboots. Daily totals are kept forever; minute-level data is kept for three months.

The processor counters measure the CPU package (cores, cache and, on some systems, memory). On machines that expose a platform-level counter, HorsePower reports whole-system power instead. Laptops without either interface fall back to the battery's power reading.
Enter your electricity tariff in Preferences to see the cost of the energy you use. Everything stays on this computer.
First release: live power with a per-component breakdown, daily and lifetime totals, one-hour history and cost estimates.
